Confirm that Anil et al.'s theorem indeed assumes zero soundness error and a deterministic verifier, as the authors state at p22 L7-L10
out.other_title: PVG: verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium iff complete and sound protocol
out.rationale: The authors do not dispute Anil et al.'s theorem under its stated assumptions but prove that the correspondence fails when those assumptions are relaxed, and say at p22 L7-L10 that its strength is severely limited by requiring zero soundness error. This is an argument that the cited result is limited, so CRITIQUES rather than CHALLENGES.
out.scope: proposed CRITIQUES: Whether equilibria of a one-message prover-verifier game correspond to valid interactive proofs; the critique applies when soundness error or randomised verifiers are allowed

text: The authors note that Anil et al. show a correspondence between equilibria of their single-message 'Abstract Decision Problem' (adp) game and valid proof systems when the prover is deterministic and the verifier mixes deterministic functions. They argue these restrictions limit the protocol's power and give Proposition 7, an adp game in which being a verifier-leading Stackelberg equilibrium is neither necessary nor sufficient for validity once the assumptions are relaxed.
title: Hammond et al. argue Anil et al.'s adp equilibrium-proof correspondence holds only narrowly
